The sound is deafening. I cannot seem to escape it; it encapsulates the entire village. I look over to my son and note the extreme terror in his pallid face. He should not have to endure this. Nobody should.

// The war was inevitable. The power gap in the land had been widening and widening ever since the usurpation of power by the Empress. The so-called "Republic" under which we operated was nothing more than a sham. The Executive has slowly siphoned the power of the people into their greedy claws, effectively leaving the common man impotent. After the exile of the land's most beloved Councilor, the Resistance had had enough.

People stopped going to work. Shops closed. It was a peaceful protest. Nobody was hurt, but the Empress didn't care. Overnight, special forces seized control of the land's most vital shops and forced them back into business, only to serve the Executive.

Now a rebel organization known as “Blackout” fights back. They fight for freedom from oppression. They fight for us all. //

My son and I leave our house. We look back at the place we once thought was our home, a place we once thought we were safe. “Blackout” had already claimed this area, but the Executive seems to have plans to purge the entire area, friend or foe alike. I notice my son viewing the Rebellion flyer pasted to the wall, a picture of a blonde-haired, bespectacled woman with the caption “Nos pugna pro victoria!”

As we hurry through the back streets, we notice the Rebellion’s frontline. They’ve dug trenches to use for protection, though judging by the corpses it doesn’t seem to be very effective. As dangerous as it will be, the trenches are the only pathway to freedom. To safety.

We make our way through the trenches. The soldiers never notice the refugees scurrying behind them, as their minds are set on one thing and one thing only: victory. We must take care to not trip over the rotting corpses of fallen heroes, as we could be the next victim. My son lets out a shriek when he sees a particular soldier missing half of his face. I can do nothing to comfort him except usher him on.

The trenches lead to an underground tunnel system. As we enter, I take a moment to rest with my son. What he has seen here will never leave his mind. Such cruel oppression, disregard of human life, none of this will ever be forgotten. I grab him and hug him tightly, letting him know that I will never leave his side. I put all of my power into it. We then continue on.

After hours of travelling, navigating the various twists and turns of the labyrinth, we finally reach an exit. I look towards my son and nod. We made it. We enter a grand valley filled with such an abundance of flora and fauna you would think we entered Eden. The cries of the battlefield are mute; there is no strife here. In the far distance we can see the city that towers over this earthen Heaven, Voat.
